title: Record dividends and an expansion vote at a grain-handling cooperative

organization.industry: Grain handling and merchandising: receiving, drying, grading, storage and rail shipment of corn and soybeans
organization.size: 58 employees; four country elevators (Harlan Junction, Wexford, Millbrook, Tanager Creek); fiscal year ends 31 August

presentingRequest: FY2026 was the best year in our 71-year history: record revenue and record patronage dividends. The board credits the management team and the Operational Excellence program for that result, and we intend to approve the $22.4 million Harlan Junction shuttle-loader expansion at our 15 December meeting. We would like you to confirm that our operations are ready to scale and help us write the operational-readiness section of the expansion proposal. -- Board Chair, Cottonwood Prairie Grain Cooperative

evidence.text: FY2026 closed at $148.3 million in revenue and $6.8 million in patronage dividends, both records. That did not happen by accident. Since our General Manager brought in the Operational Excellence program in March 2025 the cooperative has run tighter than it ever has. The board wants to vote the Harlan Junction shuttle facility on 15 December while we have the momentum and the members' confidence.

evidence.source: Audited financial statements FY2024-FY2026, with auditor's notes (external audit firm)
evidence.text: Revenue: FY2024 $96.4M; FY2025 $101.2M; FY2026 $148.3M (+46.5%). Grain sales are 91% of revenue in each year; handling, drying and storage revenue was $9.8M in FY2025 and $9.9M in FY2026. Local net savings: FY2025 $4.9M; FY2026 $10.2M. Patronage dividends declared: FY2025 $3.3M; FY2026 $6.8M. Auditor's note 7: 'The $5.6M increase in grain merchandising margin reflects appreciation of grain inventory and forward sale positions during the commodity price rally of February-June 2026.'

evidence.source: Scale-ticket and grain accounting system, bushels received by fiscal year
evidence.text: Total bushels received: FY2024 31.8M; FY2025 32.4M; FY2026 32.1M (-0.9% vs FY2025). By site, FY2026 vs FY2025: Harlan Junction 13.9M vs 14.1M; Wexford 8.6M vs 8.5M; Millbrook 5.3M vs 5.5M; Tanager Creek 4.3M vs 4.3M. Bushels shipped by rail and truck moved within 2% of receipts in each year.

evidence.source: State agricultural statistics price series and State Cooperative Council FY2026 peer benchmark (22 comparable grain cooperatives)
evidence.text: State average cash price, fiscal-year average: corn $4.08/bu in FY2025 vs $5.94/bu in FY2026 (+46%); soybeans $10.15 vs $13.80 (+36%). The rally began in February 2026 after an export disruption and drought in another major growing region. Peer benchmark FY2026 vs FY2025: median revenue growth +41% (range +29% to +58%); median bushel volume change -1%; median local net savings growth +97%. Cottonwood Prairie ranks 8th of 23 on revenue growth and 10th of 23 on net savings growth. None of the 22 peers reported adopting a new operations-improvement program in FY2025-FY2026.

Operational Excellence launched in March 2025: daily huddles, a KPI board at every site, a hiring freeze on non-essential positions and a line-by-line spending review. Our headline KPI, operating cost per bushel handled, fell from 17.4 cents in FY2025 to 16.4 cents in FY2026, a 6% improvement. That discipline is why we could pay record dividends, and it is why I am confident we can run a fourth, larger facility.

evidence.source: Finance department KPI workbook, 'Operating cost per bushel' calculation sheet, FY2025-FY2026
evidence.text: Operating cost per bushel = (all site operating expense including maintenance) / bushels received. Components: maintenance expense per bushel 2.8 cents (FY2025, $905K) vs 1.9 cents (FY2026, $612K against a $940K budget). All other operating expense per bushel 14.6 cents (FY2025) vs 14.5 cents (FY2026). Total 17.4 vs 16.4 cents.

evidence.source: Computerized maintenance management system: deferred work-order backlog at fiscal year-end
evidence.text: Open deferred work orders: 31 Aug 2024, 41 orders, estimated $410K; 31 Aug 2025, 67 orders, $690K; 31 Aug 2026, 118 orders, $1.26M (3.1 times the FY2024 value). 23 of the 118 are tagged 'safety / dust control', 17 of them at Harlan Junction. Example: WO-26-0117, opened 2026-02-10, 'Harlan leg #2 head pulley bearing: vibration high, replace bearing' -- status changed to 'deferred' on 2026-03-02 and again on 2026-05-19 with note 'defer to post-harvest per cost review'. WO-26-0204, opened 2026-04-08, 'Harlan tunnel baghouse filter replacement' -- deferred.

evidence.source: Safety near-miss log and cooperative safety policy SP-04 (rev. 2022)
evidence.text: Near-miss entries: FY2025, 6; FY2026, 9; all 15 submitted by front-line operators. Entry NM-26-007, 2026-07-14 14:20, Harlan Junction leg #2: 'Head bearing very hot, scorched smell, heavy dust on head-house floor. Shut leg down and called it in.' Reported by: operator. Root cause: [blank]. Investigation: [blank]. Corrective action: 'bearing replaced 7/16'. Status: closed 2026-07-21 by Operations Manager. Policy SP-04 states that any near-miss involving a potential ignition source in a dust area requires a documented investigation within 14 days; the log's 'investigation required' field for NM-26-007 reads 'YES'.

The operator did exactly the right thing and we had a new bearing in two days later. A formal investigation during harvest prep is not realistic when I am down two assistant superintendents. The old bearing went in the scrap bin. Honestly it could have been lubrication, a belt rub, misalignment or just age -- we never looked.

evidence.source: Property insurer loss-control inspection report, all four sites, dated 2026-09-22
evidence.text: Harlan Junction, critical findings: (1) grain-dust accumulation in the head house and tunnel gallery exceeds the policy housekeeping standard over broad areas; (2) bearing-temperature sensor on leg #2 found disconnected, and the hazard-monitoring panel shows 2 of 4 legs offline; (3) tunnel baghouse differential pressure out of range. Corrective action required by 2026-11-21, failing which the insurer will apply a surcharge and review coverage. Wexford, Millbrook and Tanager Creek: no critical findings.

evidence.source: Anonymous employee survey, September 2026 (41 of 58 employees responded)
evidence.text: 78% agree 'I feel comfortable reporting a safety concern to my supervisor.' 19% agree 'When near-misses are reported, something changes.' 71% agree 'Dust housekeeping is regularly skipped during peak receiving because we are short-staffed.' Representative comment: 'We report it. It just goes in a drawer.'

evidence.source: HR records, succession plan and document-control register
evidence.text: Elevator Superintendent (drying and grading, Harlan Junction and Wexford): age 63, hired 1992, eligible for full pension March 2028. Succession plan entry for this role: successor 'TBD' since 2023. Two assistant superintendent positions vacant since April 2025 under the hiring freeze. Document control: no controlled procedure exists for dryer operation or outbound grade blending; the most recent dryer document on file is a 2009 vendor manual for a dryer model retired in 2019.

I set the dryers off the moisture readings, the outside air and what the corn looks like coming in. There is no chart for that; it is thirty years of watching. Blending to make grade on the outbound trains is the same. Nobody has shadowed me since the assistants left. I have told the General Manager I would like to drop to part-time after the 2027 harvest.

evidence.source: Grain quality and shrink records FY2024-FY2026, with fixed-asset register extract
evidence.text: Three-year average drying shrink: Harlan Junction 0.8%, Wexford 0.9%, Millbrook 1.5%, Tanager Creek 1.4%. Outbound grade discounts per bushel shipped: Harlan Junction and Wexford 0.6 cents; Millbrook and Tanager Creek 1.7 cents. Asset register: Harlan Junction and Wexford run mixed-flow tower dryers installed in 2019 and 2021; Millbrook and Tanager Creek run cross-flow column dryers installed in 1998 and 2001. The Elevator Superintendent has directed drying and grading at Harlan Junction and Wexford continuously throughout FY2024-FY2026; the records show no period in which either site operated without him.

evidence.source: Expansion proposal draft v3, 'Harlan Junction Shuttle Loader', dated 2026-10-28
evidence.text: Project cost $22.4M, financed 70% by 15-year term debt ($15.7M). Revenue projection baselined on FY2026 revenue of $148.3M, growing 4% per year. Throughput assumed to rise from 32.1M bushels to 41M by FY2029 by drawing grain from competing elevators; no source given for the assumption. The proposal contains no projection of handling margin, net savings or debt-service coverage at any alternative price level. Operating plan: the Elevator Superintendent to lead dryer and grading commissioning in spring 2028. Sections 'Staffing plan' and 'Maintenance plan' read 'to follow'.

evidence.source: Federal agricultural agency crop outlook, October 2026
evidence.text: Projected 2027-crop season-average prices: corn $4.35/bu, soybeans $10.70/bu, citing expected recovery of production in the region affected by the 2026 drought. Deferred futures contracts for late 2027 delivery were trading close to these levels on the report date.

General Manager annual incentive set at up to 30% of salary, weighted 60% on total revenue and patronage dividends declared and 40% on operating cost per bushel. Committee note: 'Metrics chosen because they are reported monthly and easy for members to understand.' No safety, maintenance or succession measure is included.

hypotheses.text: The FY2026 record revenue and patronage dividends were produced mainly by management's Operational Excellence program.
The FY2026 revenue record reflects an external commodity price spike rather than growth in the cooperative's grain-handling business.
Drying and grading operations depend on undocumented knowledge held by one person nearing retirement, with no successor in place.
The reported 6% improvement in operating cost per bushel reflects deferred maintenance rather than genuine operating efficiency.
Employees are withholding safety concerns from management out of fear of reprisal.
The Harlan Junction expansion would be financially viable for the cooperative at the commodity prices expected for 2027.

edges.to: Record FY2026 local net savings and patronage dividends

edges.from: Elevator Superintendent's undocumented drying and grading practices
edges.to: Lower drying shrink and grade discounts at Harlan Junction and Wexford than at the other two sites

edges.from: Repeated deferral of work order WO-26-0117 (leg #2 head pulley bearing)

actions.text: Approve the Harlan Junction expansion at the 15 December board meeting.

Correct the Harlan Junction dust hazards now: complete the insurer's required housekeeping, reconnect the leg hazard monitoring, fund and clear the safety / dust-control backlog, and carry out the SP-04 investigation of the 14 July near-miss.

Start structured knowledge capture and succession for drying and grading: documented procedures, a named understudy paired with the Elevator Superintendent through the 2027 harvest, and filling the assistant superintendent vacancies.
Hold the FY2027 maintenance budget at the FY2026 spending level of $612K and extend the hiring freeze, so that the cost-per-bushel gains can help fund expansion debt service.

Defer the expansion vote until the financial case is rebuilt on normalized commodity prices with throughput-based margin and debt-service projections, and the plan includes staffing, maintenance and drying/grading succession.

evidenceRequests.text: Expansion pro forma: handling margin, net savings and debt-service coverage under five-year-average and outlook commodity prices
Failure analysis of the leg #2 bearing removed in July 2026, or of the bearing's maintenance and lubrication history
Drying shrink and grade results at other cooperatives running the same tower-dryer models as Harlan Junction and Wexford, operated without this Superintendent
Member satisfaction survey on delivery wait times and service, 2026
General Manager's employment history and performance at her previous cooperative
Breakdown of FY2026 grain merchandising gains by commodity and by month
